purpose: Fixed test material for the blind pairwise benchmark. Content is frozen here so that only design varies between methods. A method may not add, remove, or rewrite content; it may only decide layout, hierarchy, type, color, spacing, and motion.
rules_for_generation: Use every content item given. Add none.
Do not invent statistics, testimonials, logos, or prices.
No em-dash or en-dash in visible text.
The artifact must be a single self contained HTML file with inline CSS and inline JS only if needed.
Fonts: system stack or a single named family loaded from Google Fonts. No more than two families.
Deliver at a 1440px desktop viewport; include one breakpoint at 768px.

briefs.product: Postmortem, a service that turns an incident timeline into a written postmortem document
briefs.goal: Convince an engineering lead to start a 14 day trial
briefs.audience: Engineering leads at 20 to 200 person software companies who run on call rotations

headline_facts: Six hours of on call work become a document in four minutes
Reads Slack, PagerDuty, and your deploy log
Every claim it writes links to the source message
sections: Hero with the primary action and one product proof
How it works in three steps: connect sources, run the incident, receive the draft
One worked example showing a raw timeline next to the finished document
Security and data handling: what is stored, what is deleted, where it runs
Pricing logic: per seat, no per incident charge, free for teams under five
Closing action with a two line objection handler
content.required_detail: The worked example must show real looking log lines and a real looking paragraph of prose, not placeholder text

briefs.product: Kettle 03, a stovetop pour over kettle with a 0.6mm spout and a flat bottom
briefs.goal: Sell direct to consumer at 89 euros, no discount
briefs.audience: People who already brew filter coffee at home and own at least one scale

headline_facts: Gooseneck spout machined to 0.6mm for a 4mm stream
Flat bottom plate for even heat, works on induction
sections: Hero with the object large and the price stated plainly
One detail section on the spout and why 0.6mm matters, with a close view
One section on material and the three year warranty
Care instructions and what not to do with it
Shipping, returns, and the fact that it ships in four days
Closing action
content.required_detail: Because there is no photograph available, the page must communicate the object without pretending a fake photo exists. A drawn or typographic treatment of the spout dimension is expected.

briefs.product: Fleet board for a company running 240 delivery vehicles
briefs.goal: Let a dispatcher answer three questions in under five seconds: what is late, what is idle, what needs a human
briefs.audience: Dispatchers working an eight hour shift on a 27 inch monitor, plus a supervisor who checks twice a day
briefs.success_metric: Time to identify the worst performing vehicle

top_level_numbers: median delivery delay 11 minutes, up 4 from yesterday
sections: A status header with the four numbers and the time of last refresh
A ranked table of the 18 late vehicles with driver, route, minutes late, and last scan time
An idle list with the seven vehicles and how long they have been idle
An incident queue with the three items and the action each needs
A small trend view for the last 24 hours of median delay
content.required_detail: This is a working surface, not a marketing page. Density is a feature. The worst row must be findable without reading every row.

briefs.product: Billing and plan settings for a team collaboration product
briefs.goal: Let an administrator change plan, seats, and payment method without contacting support
briefs.audience: A team administrator who opens this page twice a year and is slightly anxious about money
briefs.success_metric: Completed plan change without a support ticket

sections: Current plan summary with renewal date, seat count, and monthly amount
Seat management: add or remove seats with the price consequence stated before confirmation
Plan comparison between the current plan and the one above it, limited to the differences that matter
Payment method: card on file with last four digits and an expiry warning
Invoices: a short list with date, amount, and status
Danger area: cancel the subscription, with what happens to data stated plainly
content.required_detail: Every destructive or payment action must state its consequence in the same block as the control. The user must never be surprised by a number.

briefs.product: A published research note of 2,400 words about failure rates in automated deployment
briefs.goal: Let a senior engineer read the whole note and reach the conclusion without leaving the page
briefs.audience: Senior engineers and engineering managers, reading on a laptop, often skimming first
briefs.success_metric: Completion rate and time on page

structure: A title, a one line summary, and the author with a date
A findings list of four items at the top, each one sentence
Five body sections with real headings: method, sample, the three failure classes, the cost model, and limitations
Two data tables: sample composition and cost per failure class
One chart: failure rate by deploy size, five data points
A limitations section that honestly reduces the strength of the claims
A citation list of six sources
content.required_detail: Long form reading surface. Line length, rhythm, and heading hierarchy are the design. No product marketing anywhere on the page.

briefs.product: An online companion piece for a museum exhibition about deep sea mapping
briefs.goal: Make a visitor spend four minutes moving through the piece and leave with one strong image in mind
briefs.audience: Curious general public, on a phone in a queue or on a laptop at home
briefs.success_metric: Scroll depth past the halfway point

structure: An opening statement of three lines, no image
A depth scale that runs the length of the piece, from surface to 6,000 metres, marked with five real events
Five stations, each one short paragraph and one piece of data
One moment where the visitor must act to continue, revealing the deepest station
A closing line and the exhibition details: dates, city, ticket note
content.required_detail: The depth scale is the spine of the piece. Motion is allowed here and expected, but it must serve the depth metaphor, and it must respect a reduced motion preference.
